text:
A: Hiya.
B: Hello. Tomas.
A: Joanne. Bolton.
B: Milton Keynes.
A: Right.
B: Mm.
A: Erm. What do you do?
B: Factory. Injection moulding operator. Plastic packaging.
A: Oh, same as Gary. Have you had Gary?
B: Yes. Gary is good. He talks sense. You?
A: Software. I look after a payroll system. Councils, NHS trusts, that sort of thing.
B: Payroll. Okay. Then I have question. Is true overtime is taxed more? Guys at work say they don't take extra shift because tax takes everything.
A: No. That's a myth, everyone says it. Your tax gets worked out on the month, so if you do loads of overtime one month the system sort of assumes you earn that every month, and it takes more. But it's cumulative, so it evens out over the year. If you've paid too much, it comes back to you in the next few months. The only real thing is if it actually pushes you over about fifty grand for the year, then that bit's at forty percent.
B: So they are wrong.
A: They're wrong, yeah. Unless you're on a week one or month one code. Then it doesn't even out, you'd have to sort it with HMRC.
B: How I know which code?
A: It's on your payslip. If there's a W1 or an M1 or an X after it, that's the one. If it's just 1257L you're fine.
B: I check tonight. I keep all payslips in folder. And spreadsheet.
A: Course you do. You're more organised than me. I can't find my reading glasses half the time.
B: They are on your head in photo.
A: Ha. They're probably on my head now an' all. Yeah. They are.
B: You have dog, I think. The lead, in photo.
A: Bramble. Cocker spaniel. She's daft. Gets in the bins every day, ate a loaf on Tuesday, bag and all.
B: Dogs are expensive, no? Food, vet, insurance.
A: Don't. Insurance went up again. Mark sorts that, my husband.
B: You must call and ask for lower. Always. They don't give if you don't ask.
A: That's what Gary said.
B: Gary is right.
A: You two'd get on. What do you do on your days off, then?
B: Walk around Willen Lake. Fix bikes. Watch basketball late, Lithuanian team.
A: I don't know anything about basketball.
B: Is okay. Nobody here knows. In Lithuania is like football here. More.
A: Mark's like that with Bolton Wanderers. Sits watching the scores come in like it's life or death.
B: Is life or death. Žalgiris lose again on Thursday. I am angry two days.
A: Two days. That's about what Mark does, do you know what I mean.
